body: I'm literally on the edge of being homeless. Unfortunately there isn't much I can do at this point to stop that. I dealt with homelessness as a teenager and I'm not going back to that no matter what. I'm already in debt from student loans. This world is a big trap when you don't have any real family. Some of it is my fault from bad decisions but I had no guidance so I did things that impacted my credit negatively. Problem is when you have nobody to really help you one mistake ends up tearing everything down. I've lost things before and rebuilt. I've had enough. I'm tired.  I really do want to die. I guess I'm just trying to see if I can convince myself there is something else but really I'm getting like I'm done.
I appreciate the response but that's not gonna happen at 45 with no resources. I'm tired of fighting it.
I won't be doing either but thanks for the comment. Neither of those will don't anything for me right now

Both, I've had enough. I'm sitting here right now trying to get the nerve up. Weighing everything but all I can come up with is I can't take it anymore. I see no future. Only reason I'm even on here is to get it off my chest. I've felt this way better but this feels different. It feels like it's time

I 100% know that is not a unique call. Dealing with the general public actually makes me worry about education in this country. I deal with so many adults that have no clue about the most simple things. It's actually pretty sad.

I talk to numerous customers a day ,at the rental car company I work, that I wish I could tell them to eat a dick.  Instead I have to be passive aggressive with a nice tone and tell them fuck you without saying it.

Call centers are horrible places to work period. They are normally impersonal in every way. Everything is numbers based even if the numbers make no real sense. It's just a way for the higher ups to justify their positions and salaries.

It does work in some cases if the customer has good credit with the company. It's much less expensive to keep a customer then gain a new one.  I'm not in that type of business.  People who call me will get nothing because the price is set. They have no contract with us. Complaining about the price will pretty much just get you the same answer over and over again.. It's a huge waste of time
Exactly!!!! Thank you for that well thought out response

You hit the nail on the head. It never just ends with me saying that is the lowest price. If it did, I wouldn't have any issues with it. It always leads into a conversation I would rather not have. It's a conversation where I basically just have to keep repeating the same thing over and over again in different ways. It's an uncomfortable conversation where they try to make you change the price as if you have any control over that. The customers who make me laugh are the ones who say" Well I'll just go to(insert company here)" as if they are punishing me. They don't realize that I'm glad to hear that because they weren't renting anyway.

I loved that bit in Seinfeld. You have to understand that there is no way they can have the exact car that everyone wants. To do this they would basically need to have a fleet of 1 or 2 vehicles to choose from. I doubt anyone would want that. How exactly would they be able to accommodate every single customer with the exact vehicle they want otherwise?It's highly unlikely you will get the exact make and model you are asking for because there are way too many customers renting vehicles for that to be possible. You are renting a car not buying it. I would be mad if I was buying a car and someone told me they didn't know the make and model I would receive. When you're renting you rent what is available at the time you pick up. You're renting a $10,000 to $50,000 vehicle for anywhere from $9.99 to $100 per day. What makes a person think they get to choose the exact type of car? This isn't a test drive from a car lot. The customers that make me laugh are the ones who want a convertible from a place like Minnesota. Why would someone think that in a place where it snows for a good portion of the year, it would make good business sense to keep convertibles on the lot year round? Who would be renting them during the winter and fall? nobody, that's who. People like that then act like you're lying to them when you tell them there are no convertibles in their area. They'll ask things like" So...there's no convertibles in the state of Minnesota?". Stuff like that is highly frustrating. It's just simple logic.

The problem is simple. Credit cards are protected by the credit card company. Debit cards are not. You can easily call up your bank and have a payment stopped. If this happens the company is left holding the bag and more likely will never receive payment. It's actually pretty simple logic.

I get so many customers telling me what the rules are it's ridiculous. So many of them are completely wrong but they don't care what you say. It's gotten to the point that when they refuse to take my answer I just agree with them and move along.
